Folks,

Saw this and dug into what happened — we had a similar problem with Bellwether last quarter where a forwarded invite lost its TZ anchor and effectively became a "floating" time in some calendars. Short version: Google/Outlook treat forwarded ICS files inconsistently when the DTSTART/DTEND entries don't reference a named TZ or when the organizer's calendar UID is stripped during forward. The symptom is the invite opens as-is but displays local time differently for recipients.

Options to fix before we reissue:

- Create the event in Asia/Singapore (Asia/Singapore TZ) explicitly (don't rely on the default account TZ).
- Export the ICS and edit the VTIMEZONE block so it contains a named timezone (Asia/Singapore) rather than a floating offset.
- Include a short line in the invite body with the three canonical times to avoid confusion: "09:30 SGT / 02:30 BST / 18:30 PDT" — so forwarded copies still show the right intent.

I can generate a fixed ICS and attach it. Also recommend we ask CloudFin scheduling to accept the updated invite and to avoid forwarding invites — instead they should use the scheduling inbox to add guests so the organizer's TZ isn't lost.

I'll attach a corrected ICS and a quick note on how to pin timezone in Google Calendar.

-Ben
